evidence.mission_note: A manual 2001 Z3 3.0i at the low end of the budget band directly fits the enthusiast-bridge brief. Accelerated-bridge mode still calls for a VIN check and a pre-money PPI before travelling to Albuquerque.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2001 Z3 3.0i roadster with a 5-speed manual (shifter visible), Topaz Blue over tan, Style 42 wheels, and an asking price of $11,000 OBO, near the fair-value midpoint. The seller makes specific, dated maintenance claims: a new top by House of Covers in Jan 2026 and a water pump, thermostat, upper hose and coolant in Feb 2026. None are backed by invoices, and the radiator and expansion tank are not mentioned. Observed issues are cosmetic (disclosed rear paint fade, cracked fog light, door dent, rim scrapes; worn steering-wheel leather in the photo) plus a 2021 check-engine light that was reset with no stated cause. The model's signature risk, rear subframe and trunk-floor diff-mount cracking, is entirely unaddressed. There is no VIN, so the claimed clean Carfax, the title and the odometer reading (obscured in the photo) remain unverified. Photos show a straight body, a fresh-looking top and a clean interior, but no underside or engine bay was examined here.
evidence.next_action: Email the seller for the VIN, the Carfax PDF, the cooling and top invoices, trunk-floor/diff-mount photos and tire date codes, and confirm a PPI can be done at an Albuquerque BMW independent before any deposit.
